transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-20
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Kim (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Product), Devon Clark (Solutions), Alicia Gomez (Harbor Finance - Head of Data), Marcus Lee (Harbor - Platform), Priya Nair (Harbor - Security), Tom Reynolds (CTO)
Recording ID: ff-20260620-harbor-001


00:00 Alicia: Okay great, thanks everyone for joining. We got about 40 minutes, wanting to see the console and especially usage analytics + per-route cost stuff.
00:08 Samira: Awesome, yeah we'll walk through the Console -> Usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown flow. Jonas will demo the live dashboard and we have a benchmark sheet to share.
00:20 Jonas: Hi all — I'll share my screen. Give me one sec, looks like the slides and the console are up.
00:31 (screen share starts)
00:35 Jonas: Alright, so this is the Redwood Console home. Quick note, some labels in the UI changed in the last patch, apologies if the export names differ.
00:45 Alicia: No worries, we've seen that, fine.
00:52 Jonas: First panel is aggregate usage — tokens in, tokens out, avg latency, error rate. You can filter by model, route (we call them routes for endpoints), and time range.
01:10 Jonas: For Harbor's demo we pre-populated with two routes: customer-support-chat and docs-vector-search. You can see token volumes here and a token-level cost estimate line. The cost calc is based on model profile + sequence length distribution.
01:28 Marcus: That cost per token looks higher than our own calc — what assumptions are in that estimate?
01:34 Jonas: Good q. Default assumes hosted model pricing with medium throughput profile; we include the effective per-token compute plus infra overheads and a margin. You can toggle to "Dedicated view" which will re-calc using reservation amortization and expected utilization.
01:47 Alicia: Show me that toggle.
01:50 Jonas: Sure (click). Now switched to Dedicated > you'll see per-token drops when utilization is high — that's the reserved GPU amortization. We also show breakpoints: 50%, 75%, 90% utilization to help plan commit sizes.
02:10 Priya: In Dedicated mode, do you include the additional cost for private networking and KMS?
02:15 Jonas: We put line-items for networking egress and KMS per-request if you enable Customer-managed KMS. There's a checkbox in the cost model — here under 'Security add-ons' — that adds those to the per-token price.
02:28 Tom: Do you have an option for on-prem? Our legal folks asked about air-gapped deployments.
02:33 Samira: Yes, Redwood Private is an option. The Console will show a "Private" view which omits hosted per-token costs and instead shows fixed platform fees + support + infra ops pricing. We'll send the on-prem workbook.
02:48 Jonas: Back to per-route dashboard: clicking into customer-support-chat — this shows per-minute traffic, p50/p95 latency, top prompt templates, and a token distribution histogram.
03:05 Jonas: Also a cost waterfall — token compute, batching savings (if enabled), cache hits from prefix/KV cache, and final unit cost. You can toggle quantization profile to see theoretical savings.
03:22 Alicia: That cache line — how accurate is cache hit estimation? We have lots of recurring prefixes.
03:28 Jonas: It's modeled from actual prefix matches over sampled traffic. For the demo dataset I used a 30% prefix reuse; in POC we'll run a 7‑day sample inbound and give you a revisioned estimate.
03:40 Marcus: Can we set per-route SLOs and have Redwood auto-route low-priority traffic to cheaper models when latency isn't required?
03:46 Jonas: Yes. Routing policies let you assign a route to prioritized tiers. We demoed automatic fallback in the last doc: if latency SLO is >200ms, we'll route to a cheaper quantized variant. The Console shows projected cost after policy changes.
03:58 Elena: How granular are the dashboards? Can we slice by api-key, team, or service?
04:03 Jonas: Yes, there's multi-dim filter: api_key, route, model, region, team tag. You can save views and schedule a daily export.
04:15 Alicia: Nice. Can you also show token-level cost by prompt template — we have heavy prompts with system instructions that bloat tokens.
04:23 Jonas: Yep — under 'Top prompts' you can drill down and see token counts and cost per prompt type. Here, sample prompt A (long system) is 4x the unit cost compared to short.
04:36 (brief silence, typing)
04:41 Marcus: On the export — what format? CSV? BigQuery?
04:44 Jonas: CSV, Parquet, and direct load to BigQuery or S3. Also have a webhooks option for streaming usage events.
04:54 Priya: For security reviews, we need audit logs showing who accessed which route and when. Is that in the Console?
05:01 Samira: Yes — Access + Audit tab. We log route-level access, keys, IPs, and actions. For Private customers we can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
05:14 Priya: Do you keep the logs for how long? Our retention policy is 7 years for some artifacts.
05:19 Samira: We have retention tiers — default 90 days, extended up to 7 years as an add-on. We'll include retention pricing in the SOC2 packet.
05:30 Jonas: Jumping back to the cost breakdown flow: the Console has a cost simulator. You can change batching window, enable prefix caching, choose model quantization and it recomputes cost and impact on latency in real-time.
05:50 Jonas: For example, enabling moderate batching (50 ms) reduces per-token cost by about 18% on the sample but increases p95 by ~15ms — tradeoff visible in the 'Impact' panel.
06:03 Alicia: Is that batching compatible with streaming responses? We need streaming for chat.
06:08 Jonas: Good catch — streaming and aggressive batching can conflict. We show compatibility — small-batch streaming allowed up to X tokens; for long streaming responses we recommend caching + prefix optimization instead.
06:20 Marcus: For the POC we want to run benchmarks: 1) hosted baseline, 2) dedicated reserved instance at 70% util, 3) private on-prem prototype. Can you run those?
06:28 Samira: Absolutely. We'll propose a benchmark plan in the pilot proposal. Jonas will lead the hosted vs dedicated runs, and our infra folks can partner on private runs.
06:35 Jonas: I'll share the benchmark spreadsheet after this call — it has the required payloads, sample rate, and result templates.
06:41 Alicia: Great. Please include the top 10 routes by volume; Marcus will populate those on Monday.
06:46 Marcus: Yep, will do.
06:48 (5 second crosstalk)
06:54 Tom: A couple legal/security Qs — can you walk through encryption at rest and KMS integration?
07:02 Priya: And SSO? We need SAML/SCIM support.
07:05 Samira: Sure — at a high level: we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, where keys never leave your KMS; we support envelope encryption for hosted as an option. We also offer SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, and per-route role filters.
07:25 Jonas: I'll drop the SOC2 + network diagram link in the chat. The SOC2 doc details encryption, key management, and access controls.
07:34 Jonas: Link: https://redwood.com/security/soc2 (note: demo link)
07:40 Priya: Thanks. We'll want a TLS diagram and what endpoints we expect to open.
07:44 Samira: We'll include that in the network workbook.
07:48 Alicia: Back to observability — can we compare model variants side-by-side in the Console? Eg gpt-small-quant vs gpt-medium?
07:55 Jonas: Yes — 'Compare' mode lets you overlay latency, quality metrics (if you upload evals), and cost. We will also surface regression alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold tied to your eval set.
08:08 Elena: How do we upload evals? Is it per-route?
08:12 Jonas: You can upload a CSV of prompts + expected outputs, then tag to routes. The Console will run periodic sampling and show rouge/approx similarity scores.
08:22 Alicia: What's the easiest way to see where cost is coming from next month — we need a one-pager to show CFO.
08:27 Jonas: There's a 'Monthly Cost Summary' export that aggregates per-route, per-team, and highlights top 5 cost drivers and savings opportunities (batching, caching, model swaps).
08:36 Samira: We'll include a sample one-pager in the deck.
08:40 (Jonas posts: Slides: https://app.redwood.ai/slides/console-walkthrough ; Benchmarks: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/harbor-poc )
08:51 Marcus: Great, got the links.
08:54 Alicia: On multi-region routing — we have EU data residency needs. Can you show how Console displays region split?
08:59 Jonas: Sure. In the per-route view select region split — you'll see traffic & cost per region. You can pin a route to EU-only and the router will only send to EU-hosted replicas; cost model recomputes accordingly.
09:12 Priya: If a user in US hits an EU-only route, do you reject or route and log?
09:17 Jonas: Policies are configurable: reject, warn+log, or route via an anonymizing proxy (with compliance note). We usually recommend reject + clear UX error for strict residency.
09:27 Tom: For our pilot, timeline is: get pilot proposal, sign, run tests over two weeks, then present results. Is that feasible?
09:34 Samira: Yes, that timeline looks good. Pilot scope typically 2 weeks for hosted vs dedicated; private can take longer depending on infra access.
09:42 Alicia: Okay, last question — pricing model for dedicated: are there committed usage tiers or flat monthly slots?
09:49 Samira: We offer reserved GPU pools with monthly/annual commits. The Console will show estimated effective cost per token based on commit size and utilization; we'll include a pricing table in the proposal.
09:59 Marcus: Can you show an example of commit size effect?
10:02 Jonas: (navigates) Here's a chart: commit 4x GPUs at 70% util gives $X per million tokens; at 40% util it's much higher. We also show recommended burst capacity and autoscale buffers.
10:18 Alicia: Perfect.
10:22 (brief pause)
10:27 Samira: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: 1) Samira sends pilot + pricing proposal by Tues (2026-06-23). 2) Jonas shares benchmark sheet and infra templates by Mon (2026-06-22). 3) Marcus provides list of top routes and token volumes by Mon. 4) Priya sends compliance contacts and questions by Wed. We'll schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-06-29.
10:54 Tom: That works — thanks everyone.
10:59 Alicia: Thanks, this was helpful.
